examples.label: Wildcard both login fields to bypass the LDAP filter
ldapsearch reference for valid query syntax

notes: A bare * in both fields matches every entry when the app concatenates input straight into the filter. If * is filtered, try )(cn=* style breakouts. Confirms when a wildcard logs you in as the first user.

recommended.note: Another application-logic web vuln in this module.

name: LDAP Injection - Authentication Bypass
description: When login builds an LDAP filter like (&(sAMAccountName=$user)(userPassword=$pass)), injecting the wildcard * matches any entry, bypassing authentication. Test * in each field.

defense.why_it_works: LDAP authentication queries that concatenate user-supplied values directly into the filter string are vulnerable to injection. Supplying a wildcard (*) as username causes the filter to match any user, bypassing authentication entirely.
defense.prerequisites: Application using LDAP for authentication with string-concatenated filter construction. No input sanitization or parameterized LDAP queries.
defense.impact: Authentication bypass -- attacker logs in as any user (often the first user, potentially an admin). Full application access without valid credentials.
defense.detection: Login attempts with wildcard characters (* or %) in username or password. Successful authentication for a wildcard username. LDAP server log showing filter with unescaped wildcards.
defense.artifacts: Application auth log (wildcard username succeeding) | LDAP server audit log (filter with * in uid field) | Web server log (POST to login with * in parameters)
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web sourcetype=access_combined (uri_query=\"**)(*\" OR uri_path=\"**)(*\" OR uri_query=\"**))%00*\" OR uri_path=\"**))%00*\" OR uri_query=\"**)(uid=**\" OR uri_path=\"**)(uid=**\" OR uri_query=\"*%2a%29*\" OR uri_path=\"*%2a%29*\")
| table _time, clientip, uri_path, uri_query, status
defense.elastic_kql: event.category:web AND (url.query:(**)(* OR **))%00* OR **)(uid=** OR *%2a%29*) OR url.path:(**)(* OR **))%00* OR **)(uid=** OR *%2a%29*))
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem has_any ("*)(", "*))%00", "*)(uid=*", "%2a%29") or csUriQuery has_any ("*)(", "*))%00", "*)(uid=*", "%2a%29")
| project TimeGenerated, cIP, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// ldap_injection
defense.sigma_rules: web_ldap_injection (malicious request pattern in web logs)
defense.prevention: Use LDAP libraries with parameterized queries or bind variables. Escape all special LDAP characters per RFC 4515 before inserting into filters. Validate input against an allowlist of alphanumeric characters.
defense.misconfiguration: Application builds LDAP filter by string concatenation without escaping LDAP special characters (* ( ) \ NUL).
defense.evasion: Try variations: %)(%)(uid=* or injecting OR conditions (|(uid=admin)).

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review IIS Web Server logs, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Bypasses an LDAP-backed login by injecting a wildcard:
  Username: *   matches any account entry
  Password: *   matches any password value
If the login builds a filter like (&(sAMAccountName=$user)(userPassword=$pass)), the * makes the filter match any entry and authentication succeeds; test * (and other LDAP metacharacters) in each field.
